**🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration** | **🟠 Major** | **🏗️ Heavy lift**

**Preserve content-block order when accumulating tool calls.**

If Nova emits text between two tool calls, both accumulators retain the tool calls in `tool_blocks` but merge all text into `outputText`. The Amazon span mapper then places that merged text before both tool calls. The exported message no longer represents the response order. Retain ordered content blocks, using `contentBlockIndex` to associate deltas with their blocks, and emit parts in that order. AWS documents multiple tool calls and content-block indices. ([docs.aws.amazon.com](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/tool-use-invocation.html?utm_source=openai))

  


Also applies to: 200-202

Merge Risk: Low · up to f0322

Streamed Nova tool calls and finish reasons are now captured in spans. When a response interleaves text between tool calls, the exported span may show the text before all of the tool calls. This matches the existing Converse behavior and can be fixed in a follow-up, so the change is mergeable with that known limitation.
Security architecture risk: Moderate · up to e0166

Newly captured tool arguments can appear in diagnostic logs even when content tracing is disabled. Exposure requires debug logging to be enabled and collected; normal response-content export remains protected by the existing setting. **Retained concerns** - **Medium · security · observed:** Synchronous streaming can disclose newly accumulated tool arguments through debug logs even with TRACELOOP_TRACE_CONTENT=false and no content-tracing override. The logger prints the accumulator before each event, so events following an input delta expose previously accumulated arguments. The logging statement predates this PR, but its tool-argument exposure is newly introduced. Actual disclosure requires DEBUG logging and collection of these records.
Security review details

**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The diagnostic-log exposure covers accumulated tool arguments processed by synchronous wrappers in a DEBUG-enabled process. Confidentiality impact depends on argument sensitivity, log collection, and reader access. The asynchronous accumulator has no corresponding debug statement, and the inspected path does not execute tools or grant additional authority. **Security Findings and Attack Paths** - _observed_ — Tool-use input arrives in provider response chunks, is decoded and appended to tool_blocks, and is included in the next synchronous accumulator debug record. This route does not consult the content-tracing setting or require a recording span. The base retained neither these input deltas nor their accumulated arguments, although it already logged text and other accumulator fields. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The strongest counterevidence is that disabling content tracing still prevents tool arguments from entering response-message span attributes. The inspected response-event emitter also does not serialize tool_blocks. The identified control gap is the separate synchronous diagnostic-log sink, not the normal gated span-output path. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — Each wrapper initializes its own accumulator. Async iteration guards completion against duplicate callbacks and uses finally; synchronous completion occurs on iterator exhaustion. These existing lifecycle differences do not establish cross-stream leakage or additional tool authority, but interrupted and repeated tool-use sequences remain incompletely covered.
